rules.sentence: Diagnosis of LBD requires thorough clinical examination as many of its features overlap with other dementia disorders.
The latest LBD consortium has set an arbitrary 12-month rule to differentiate LBD from Parkinson disease with dementia.

If the patient has Parkinson disease for 12 months or longer before any cognitive impairment is noticed, then the disorder is most likely Parkinson disease with dementia, if the time period is shorter then the disorder is LBD.
In most cases of LBD, dementia precedes motor signs, particularly episodes of diminished responsiveness and visual hallucinations.

If the patient has Parkinson disease for 12 months or longer before any cognitive impairment is noticed, then the disorder is most likely Parkinson disease with dementia, if the time period is shorter then the disorder is LBD.
